subject: biology
title: Eukaryotic and prokaryotic cells
key_idea: Animal and plant cells are **eukaryotic**: their DNA is enclosed in a nucleus. Bacterial cells are **prokaryotic**: they are much smaller and their DNA is not in a nucleus. Each structure inside a cell has a job, and cells are measured in micrometres.

blocks.text: All living things are made of cells, and there are two types. This section covers what each type contains.

items.meaning: A cell whose DNA is enclosed in a nucleus (animals, plants, fungi).
A cell with no nucleus (bacteria). Much smaller than a eukaryotic cell.
The part of the cell that contains the DNA.
A small ring of extra DNA, separate from the main loop.

items: Cell membrane
Cytoplasm
Genetic material enclosed in a **nucleus**
Cell membrane and cytoplasm, surrounded by a **cell wall**
One loop of DNA, free in the cytoplasm (no nucleus)
Often one or more **plasmids**
Some have a flagellum, a tail-like structure that makes the cell move
Eukaryotic cells have a nucleus. Prokaryotic cells do not.
Bacterial DNA is a single loop in the cytoplasm, plus plasmids.
Bacterial cells are much smaller.

blocks.text: Each sub-cellular structure has one job. The table gives the job and where it is found.

rows: Contains the DNA and controls the activities of the cell
Controls which substances enter and leave the cell
Where aerobic respiration happens, which releases energy
Contain chlorophyll, which absorbs light for photosynthesis
Plant cells only (not all of them)
Supports and strengthens the cell. In plants it is made of cellulose
Filled with cell sap. Helps keep the cell firm

items: A bacterial cell wall is **not** made of cellulose.
Bacterial ribosomes are smaller than eukaryotic ribosomes.
Mitochondria and chloroplasts are found only in eukaryotic cells.

diagram.alt: A table comparing animal, plant and bacterial cells. Animal and plant cells are eukaryotic with a nucleus and mitochondria. Plant cells also have chloroplasts, a cellulose cell wall and a permanent vacuole. Bacterial cells are prokaryotic, much smaller, with a loop of DNA, plasmids and a cell wall that is not cellulose.
items: Animal cell
Plant cell
Bacterial cell
Mitochondria release energy by aerobic respiration.
Ribosomes make proteins. Chloroplasts carry out photosynthesis.
Chloroplasts, a cellulose wall and a permanent vacuole identify a plant cell.

blocks.text: Cells are far too small to measure in metres, so we use unit prefixes and powers of ten.

items.meaning: A word-start that changes the size of a unit, such as milli or micro.
A number written as a × 10ⁿ, where a is between 1 and 10.
A power of ten. Used to compare how many times bigger one thing is than another.

items: Millimetres to micrometres: multiply by 1000.
Micrometres to millimetres: divide by 1000.
Example: 0.07 mm × 1000 = 70 µm.

blocks.label: How many times bigger
blocks.formula: number of times bigger = larger size ÷ smaller size
where: Both sizes must be in the same unit.
Round the answer to the nearest power of ten to give the order of magnitude.

items.text: A plant cell is 100 µm. A bacterial cell is 1 µm.
100 = 10², so the plant cell is two orders of magnitude bigger.

items: Cells are measured in micrometres (µm): 1 mm = 1000 µm.
Convert both sizes to the same unit before comparing.
Give an order of magnitude as a power of ten.

checks.q: Describe where the genetic material is found in a bacterial cell.
checks.a: The DNA is not in a nucleus. It is a single loop free in the cytoplasm, and there may also be plasmids (small rings of DNA).

checks.q: Give the function of the mitochondria.
checks.a: They are where aerobic respiration happens, which releases energy.

checks.q: A bacterial cell is 0.002 mm long. Write its length in micrometres and in metres using standard form.
checks.a: 0.002 mm × 1000 = 2 µm. In metres it is 2 × 10⁻⁶ m.

worked_example.question: Describe four differences between a bacterial cell and a plant cell.
answer_points: The bacterial cell is smaller than the plant cell.
The bacterial cell does not have its DNA inside a nucleus. The plant cell does.
The bacterial cell may have plasmids. The plant cell does not.
The bacterial cell does not have chloroplasts or mitochondria. The plant cell has both.
The cell wall in a bacterial cell is not made of cellulose. The plant cell wall is.
The bacterial cell does not have a large permanent vacuole. The plant cell does.
worked_example.tip: Any four of these score one mark each. Name both cells so the difference is clear.

worked_example.question: Bacterial cells contain plasmids. Describe three other features of a bacterial cell.
answer_points: It has no nucleus. The chromosomal DNA is in the cytoplasm.
It has a cell wall.
It may have a flagellum.
It has ribosomes.
It has no membrane-bound organelles, so no mitochondria.
worked_example.tip: Any three score one mark each. A slime capsule or pili would also be credited. Cell membrane and cytoplasm are ignored.

worked_example.question: Compare the DNA found in eukaryotic and in prokaryotic cells.
answer_points: In eukaryotes the DNA is contained in the nucleus.
In prokaryotes the DNA is in the cytoplasm.
In eukaryotes the DNA is a strand, but in prokaryotes it is a loop.
Prokaryotes have plasmids and eukaryotes do not.
In both, the DNA is made of the same parts: bases, sugar and phosphate.
worked_example.tip: Any three score one mark each. Compare means both cells appear in each point.

worked_example.question: Describe differences and similarities between the structure of a plant root hair cell and a bacterial cell.
answer_points: Differences (maximum 3): the root hair cell has a nucleus, mitochondria and a large permanent vacuole.
The root hair cell wall is made of cellulose.
The root hair cell has linear DNA and no plasmids.
Similarities (maximum 3): both have a cell wall, a cell membrane and cytoplasm.
Both have ribosomes and DNA (genetic material).
Five marks in total from the differences and similarities.
worked_example.tip: Give at least two similarities as well as differences, because the marks are shared between both.
